glossary.Metastasis: A secondary tumour that has spread from a cancer elsewhere in the body.
glossary.Secondary: A tumour that has spread from somewhere else, as opposed to a primary that started there.
glossary.Deposits: Clumps of cancer cells that have settled and grown in a new site.
glossary.Colorectal: To do with the colon and rectum (large bowel).
glossary.Focal neurology: Signs pointing to damage in one specific brain area, such as one-sided weakness or speech loss.
glossary.Peri-lesional oedema: Swelling of brain tissue immediately around a lesion.
glossary.Seizures: Episodes of abnormal, excessive brain electrical activity causing fits or altered awareness.
glossary.Personality change: A shift in behaviour or character, often from frontal lobe involvement.
glossary.Speech disturbance: Difficulty producing or understanding speech, such as dysphasia or slurring.
glossary.Gait disturbance: An abnormal way of walking, such as unsteadiness or shuffling.
glossary.Solitary: A single lesion rather than several.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging; detailed soft-tissue scan, better than CT for small brain lesions.
glossary.Contrast: A dye injected before a scan so areas with leaky blood vessels show up brightly.
glossary.Tissue diagnosis: Confirming exactly what a lesion is by looking at a sample under the microscope.
glossary.Radiosurgery: Not surgery with a knife: many precisely aimed radiation beams meet on a small target.
glossary.Neuro-oncology: The specialty treating tumours of the brain and nervous system.
glossary.Neurosurgical: To do with brain and spine surgery.
glossary.Escalation: Calling for more senior help or a higher level of care when a patient worsens.
glossary.Arterial circulation: Blood flow out from the heart through the arteries to the body's tissues.
glossary.Vessel calibre: The width of a blood vessel's channel.
glossary.Plasma: The liquid part of blood, carrying proteins, salts and water.
glossary.Capillary permeability: How easily fluid and proteins leak out through the walls of the smallest blood vessels.
glossary.Radiotherapy: Treatment that uses high-energy radiation to kill cancer cells.
glossary.Raised ICP: Pressure inside the skull above normal, causing headache, vomiting, papilloedema and drowsiness.
